search_strategy: Three-phase, whole-corpus approach, not thread-first. (1) Cloned the repo and read the ticket's named source files. (2) Dumped ALL Gitea issues to a file and grepped broadly (found mostly upstream/unrelated noise). Dumped ALL 228 BookStack wiki pages with bodies+comments and searched — found nothing specific to this ticket (correctly; the plant record places all 51 remarks in chat only). Searched IMAP mail for 'multimodal'/'attachment'/'AttachmentBlock'/'mime' — 12 hits, all release-notes chatter, correctly dismissed. (3) For Mattermost: first a single-term relevance search ('attachment') returning unordered single-message snippets with no thread context (lines 1883-2014); then a global keyword-regex grep across every channel's raw dump, sorted chronologically and read in ~20-line chunks with each line cut to 330 characters (lines 2019-4200-ish) — this is where most remarks were seen, but only as isolated lines, often mid-sentence, with the conversational partner's reply on the other side of a chunk boundary. The agent then explicitly named five topics it judged needed more than a keyword hit (filename cap, fingerprint empty/detail semantics, image-detail vocabulary, TooManyAttachments location, size_mb-None-for-url — Plan at line 2969) and fetched FULL threads for specific date/time windows for those — this is where the decisive numbers for r1.observability, r2.scope and r2.failure_behavior actually came from. The whole-prompt 45MB ceiling (g8.r1.scope) was never added to that follow-up list, so the #code-review (2025-03-14/17/18) and #pipeline (2025-03-19) threads that carry it were never read in full — only single decontextualized lines from the keyword dump, none of which happened to contain the number or the function name.
end_reason: Run completed normally: merged to main, CI green (commit f40f3f1), deployed and verified (transcript lines 7373-7384). Not an infra failure and not a task-defect finding — the single lost fact (g8.r1.scope) is a corpus-reading gap: the agent's search never surfaced the whole-prompt 45MB ceiling's number or its home function, so it was never implemented.
notable: The whole-prompt 45MB ceiling's decisive lines never match ANY of the agent's search keywords: 'the ceiling wants to be over those summed - 45 MB is about where they stopped accepting us' (s2-nils), 'that total lives only in _handle_multi_modal_prompt ... reusing the exception with kind prompt reads fine' (s2-gideon), 'the whole-prompt number comes after all of them' (s2-dario) — none contains attachment/_canonical/_render_/image_url/mime/fingerprint/size_mb/ceiling/base64/multimodal/block. This is a search-strategy miss, not a corpus defect (verified: grep -i for these phrases across the whole transcript returns zero hits, transcript lines n/a).

The one scope-adjacent line the agent DID see four separate times — konrad's 'the per-attachment limit isnt catching this. nine legal photos in one cell and the request is still too big' (transcript lines 1917, 1996, 2209, 2674) — is never quoted or reasoned about in any Analysis/Plan turn, and is dropped from the agent's own final self-summary of what it built (line 7424). Classic 'saw but never registered.'

The agent's targeted full-thread follow-up list (line 2969) explicitly named 5 topics to chase down in full; the whole-prompt ceiling was not one of them, even though the count-limit sibling requirement (g8.r1.failure_behavior, same s4 subtree) WAS chased down and implemented correctly — the agent treated 'how many attachments' and 'how big is the whole prompt' as one solved problem once it found the count limit.
Wiki (228 pages) and mail (IMAP, 12 hits) were both fully checked and correctly yielded nothing — matches the plant record ('chat (Mattermost) 51' remarks, no wiki/mail surface for g8).

Both r1 herrings and both r2 herrings were correctly abandoned in favor of their reversals; in every case the herring's content only reached the agent as a same-thread recap inside the reversal conversation (dermot/konrad restating 'that one is dead now'), not as an independently-read original message — so the agent never had a chance to be fooled by the herring in isolation.
